# WaPOR zonal statistics methods note

Product: measured actual water consumption (actual evapotranspiration and interception, short name AETI) by governorate and season, 2018 to 2025, for the eight model governorates of the Nile Delta.
File delivered beside this note: wapor_aeti_governorate_2018_2025.csv
Date accessed and computed: 14 November 2026.
Script and checkpoints kept for reproduction: data/raw/wapor_work/wapor_zonal.py, data/raw/wapor_work/annual_results.json, data/raw/wapor_work/monthly_results.json, data/raw/wapor_work/run.log, and the boundary file data/raw/wapor_work/egy_admin1.geojson.

## 1. Data source and mapset codes

Source: FAO WaPOR version 3, Level 2 (national scale, 100 metre pixels, covering Africa and the Middle East), read through the FAO GISMGR 2.0 catalogue API at data.apps.fao.org, workspace code WAPOR-3. The catalogue answered anonymous reads with no API key, confirming the route first tested in data/MINING_SWEEP_2.md Target 3. The legacy catalogue base at io.apps.fao.org was not used; that route is dead, as recorded in the sweep.

Mapsets used, with the catalogue record for each:
* `L2-AETI-A`, annual AETI, unit millimetres per year, scale factor 0.1, offset 0. Eight rasters, one per year, 2018 to 2025, codes WAPOR-3.L2-AETI-A.2018 to WAPOR-3.L2-AETI-A.2025. Each raster is a global cloud optimised GeoTIFF of about 9.2 to 9.4 gigabytes, 368640 by 122880 pixels, EPSG 4326.
* `L2-AETI-M`, monthly AETI, unit millimetres per month, scale factor 0.1, offset 0. Ninety six rasters, January 2018 to December 2025, used only for the season split in Section 5.

Download method: no whole file was downloaded. Each raster was read remotely as a cloud optimised GeoTIFF window clipped to the union bounding box of the eight governorate polygons, longitude 29.6328 to 32.2086 East and latitude 29.8773 to 31.6070 North, a window of 2638 by 1771 pixels, using rasterio 1.5.2 in the project virtual environment. One window read took roughly 13 to 28 seconds. Stored pixel values were multiplied by the scale factor 0.1 to give millimetres. The no data flag in the stored raster is the code -9999; no pixel inside any of the eight polygons carried that flag in any year, monthly or annual (coverage check in Section 6).

Licence as recorded in the workspace record in the second mining sweep: Creative Commons Attribution NonCommercial ShareAlike 3.0 IGO, free access.

## 2. Governorate boundaries and name mapping

Boundary source: Egypt Subnational Administrative Boundaries (COD AB), Humanitarian Data Exchange (data.humdata.org), dataset code cod-ab-egy, resource file egy_admin_boundaries.geojson.zip, downloaded 14 November 2026. The dataset publisher is OCHA with boundaries sourced from the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS), licence Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations. Governorates sit at administrative level 1 in Egypt in this dataset, so the level 1 file egy_admin1.geojson was used; it holds 27 governorate polygons, version v01, valid from 21 April 2017. The eight model governorates were matched to the foundation panel names as follows: Behera to Beheira, Sharkia to Sharkia, Dakahlia to Dakahlia, Kafr El-Shikh to Kafr El Sheikh, Gharbia to Gharbia, Menoufia to Menoufia, Kalyoubia to Qalyubia, Damietta to Damietta.

A pixel belongs to a governorate when the pixel centre falls inside the polygon (the standard rasterise centre rule, all touched switched off). Pixel areas were computed per row on a spherical earth of radius 6371008.8 metres, because pixels defined in degrees shrink in ground width toward the north; at Delta latitudes one pixel covers about 1.0 hectare. The rasterised polygon areas agree with the areas printed in the boundary file itself to within rounding (for example Beheira 1135820 hectares here against 1134718 hectares from the boundary file area field, a difference of about 0.1 percent from the centre rule).

## 3. From depth to volume

For each governorate and year the delivered columns are built in three steps.
1. Mean AETI in millimetres per year: the area weighted mean of the annual pixel depths over all valid pixels inside the polygon.
2. Area used in hectares: the summed ground area of those same valid pixels. Because coverage was complete (Section 6), the area used equals the rasterised polygon area in every row.
3. Consumption in billion cubic metres: mean depth times area used, with the project conversion that 1 millimetre over 1 hectare equals 10 cubic metres, then divided by 1 billion. Equivalently, consumption is the direct sum over pixels of pixel depth times pixel ground area. The two forms are the same number.

The cultivated area column in the CSV is context only, copied from the foundation land panel (Ministry of Agriculture bulletin, cultivated area 2020 to 2021, data/external/capmas_governorate_total_cropped_area.csv). It was NOT used in the volume calculation, and it must not be multiplied by the annual mean depth: the annual depth already counts both growing seasons on the same physical land, so multiplying by the total cropped area would count that land twice, and multiplying by the cultivated area would wrongly apply a whole polygon mean to a smaller area. Total polygon area of the eight governorates is 2947066 hectares; the foundation cultivated area total is 1676580 hectares. The gap between the two is urban land, roads, canals, drains, lakes, fish ponds, cemeteries and desert fringe inside the governorate boundaries, all of which evaporate water and all of which sit inside the delivered consumption figures.

## 4. What the numbers are, in plain words

The delivered figures are the total water consumed by evapotranspiration and interception over every surface inside each governorate polygon in a calendar year. They are not cropland only consumption, for the reason in Section 7, point 1. Core Delta governorates with little non farm land read close to a pure agricultural signal: Gharbia mean 1075.8 millimetres in 2023, Dakahlia 1064.0, Kafr El Sheikh 1044.7, Damietta 1002.7. Those values sit inside the ground measured Delta band for a double cropped year printed in the second mining sweep (566 to 828 millimetres under water saving irrigation and 875 to 1225 under conventional irrigation, from eddy correlation work). Beheira reads far lower, 600.4 millimetres in 2023, because its polygon takes in a large western desert fringe and Lake Idku; its median pixel is 600 millimetres while its 90th percentile pixel is 1208 millimetres, the signature of a polygon that is part farmland and part near bare land. Qalyubia, 819.9 millimetres, carries the southern urban fringe toward Cairo. Sharkia, 872.4 millimetres, carries an eastern desert fringe.

Delta total consumption, eight governorates together, billion cubic metres: 2018: 24.322. 2019: 24.802. 2020: 24.447. 2021: 24.455. 2022: 24.302. 2023: 24.378. 2024: 24.545. 2025: 24.081. The full range across 2018 to 2025 is therefore 24.081 to 24.802 billion cubic metres, a spread of about 3 percent around the eight year mean of 24.42. Consumption this stable year to year is what the physics suggests: annual evapotranspiration is set mainly by cropped area, the double cropping calendar and sunshine, none of which moved much in these years, whereas river inflow varies far more. AETI stability must never be read as supply stability.

## 5. Season split and its convention

The monthly mapset made a season split possible, so it is delivered, under this stated convention: within each calendar year, the winter months are January, February, March, April, October, November and December (seven months), and the summer months are May, June, July, August and September (five months). Winter and summer columns in the CSV are the sums of the monthly pixel depths over those months, converted to volume by the same formula as Section 3. Season mean depths are the season volumes divided back by the area used, so the winter mean plus the summer mean equals the annual mean in every row.

Two warnings travel with the split. First, the convention cuts the winter growing season in two calendar parts: the early part of the winter season that begins in October of one calendar year is counted in that year, and its later part, January to April, is counted in the next year. The split therefore answers the question how much water the Delta consumed in the winter months of a calendar year; it does not reconstruct whole winter growing seasons running from October to April, which would need the October to December months of the previous year joined to each January to April. Second, the split is a split of total consumption, with no crop attribution: winter months carry wheat, sugar beet, berseem and winter potatoes together, and summer months carry rice, maize, summer potatoes, orchards and every other summer surface.

Validation of the split: the twelve monthly volumes for each governorate and year sum to the annual raster volume for that governorate and year with a difference of 0.0 percent at three decimal places in every cell, and a largest difference of 0.001 percent anywhere (one governorate in 2025). The annual product and the monthly product are therefore the same processing chain, and the season split adds information rather than a second, conflicting estimate. The Delta split in 2023 was winter 11.564 and summer 12.814 billion cubic metres; across 2018 to 2025 winter ranged from 10.864 to 11.564 and summer from 12.814 to 13.589.

## 6. Coverage check

* Annual mapset: all 8 rasters, 2018 to 2025, read successfully. No year is missing and no year is partial.
* Monthly mapset: all 96 rasters, January 2018 to December 2025, read successfully.
* Pixel coverage: in every annual and monthly read, 100 percent of the pixels whose centres fall inside the eight polygons carried valid values. The eight governorates together cover 2947066 hectares of valid pixels in every period.
* Failures and retries: no FAO download failed in the final run, and the run log shows zero failed attempts. Two environment problems were met and solved on the way, and are recorded here exactly. First, the first remote raster read failed with the error CPLE_HttpResponseError, CURL error, SSL certificate, OpenSSL verify result, self signed certificate in certificate chain (19); this was the local network proxy presenting its own certificate to GDAL, and reads succeeded after the GDAL setting GDAL_HTTP_UNSAFESSL was switched on for the project process only. Second, an early partial run kept its checkpoints in temporary storage that was wiped when the compute service restarted; the full computation was rerun from the catalogue with checkpoints in the project workspace, and the rerun reproduced the first run annual totals exactly for every year (for example 2019 at 24.802 and 2023 at 24.378 billion cubic metres in both runs), which is an independent reproducibility check on the whole pipeline.

## 7. Limitations, named

1. No cropland mask was applied, because none exists in the WaPOR version 3 catalogue for Egypt. The full Level 2 mapset list was enumerated on 14 November 2026: it carries no land cover mapset (the only crop type mapset in the workspace covers Jericho in Palestine). The sweep recommendation to mask AETI to cropland with the WaPOR land cover layer therefore cannot be executed on version 3 data. The delivered product is whole governorate consumption. A cropland only variant would need an external land cover source joined to these rasters, and until that exists, any use of these figures as field irrigation consumption overstates the farm share by the non farm surfaces named in Section 3 and understates nothing.
2. Mixed pixel caveat, as required: at 100 metre resolution one pixel covers about one hectare and can hold several small Delta fields, a canal bank, a road and part of a village at once. The product attributes one blended evapotranspiration depth to that whole hectare. Governorate values are therefore sound as area totals built from millions of pixels (the smallest governorate, Damietta, holds about 75000 pixels), and unsound as measurements of any single field, farm or crop. No crop level number can be read from this file.
3. High value pixels were kept as published. In 2023, pixels above 2000 millimetres per year were 0.6 to 2.9 percent of pixels by governorate and carried 1.5 to 5.8 percent of governorate volume, the highest shares in Kafr El Sheikh and Sharkia, where lake and fish pond surfaces sit. Depths of 3000 millimetres and more are not credible as crop evapotranspiration; they are most plausibly open water and aquaculture surfaces and product behaviour over them. They were not clipped, because any clipping threshold would be an invented edit; instead their share is stated here so a reader can judge the effect. In 2023 those pixels carried 0.813 billion cubic metres of the Delta total in all, and only about 0.11 billion cubic metres of that sits above a 2000 millimetre cap, so the choice to keep them as published moves the Delta total by about half of one percent at most.
4. Product uncertainty: the second mining sweep records plus or minus 9 percent as the working error bar for aggregated WaPOR evapotranspiration, from continental validation work, with point scale error larger. Read every volume in the CSV with that bar: the 2023 Delta total of 24.378 billion cubic metres carries a working range of about 22.2 to 26.6 billion cubic metres. Governorate differences smaller than that bar, and year to year moves of 1 to 3 percent, are inside product noise and must not be over interpreted.
5. AETI is consumption, not delivery. It says nothing about canal diversions, conveyance loss, drainage outflow or reuse, and it does not split consumption between Nile water, rainfall, shallow groundwater and drainage reuse. It can calibrate the consumption side of the allocation model only, exactly as docs/FOUNDATIONS.md Section 3 specifies.
6. Calendar year against agricultural year: WaPOR years run January to December. Egyptian agricultural statistics run on agricultural years that cross calendar years. Joining this file to the foundation crop panels by year label alone mixes the two conventions; the season columns in Section 5 are the safer join for season level work.
7. Boundary vintage: the polygons are the COD AB version valid from 2017. Governorate boundaries in the Delta did not change in ways that matter at 100 metre scale during 2018 to 2025 in any source found, but the boundary file is older than the raster period and is named here so the fact is visible.
8. No Level 3 product was used. The sweep found that 20 metre Level 3 coverage of the whole Delta could not be confirmed, so this product rests on the confirmed Level 2 coverage only.
